content: Homelessness and housing insecurity create significant challenges for individuals managing diabetes. These challenges include the lack of access to safe and reliable storage for insulin and other necessary medical supplies, which are critical for effective diabetes care. People experiencing homelessness or unstable housing conditions are also more likely to suffer from food insecurity, which can make it difficult to maintain a consistent and appropriate diet for blood sugar control. Additionally, this population often has lower levels of health literacy, which can hinder their ability to understand and follow diabetes management plans. Furthermore, they experience higher rates of cognitive impairments and behavioral health disorders, which can further complicate their ability to manage their condition effectively.
